role: Seven individual complete original harness/API reviews on the 21.x legacy add-on

reviews.decision: The original commit adds public content-loader methods to the modern MDC option harness. The owned legacy option harness retains its untouched Material16 class implementation and public parent. Adding those methods is outside the finite historical legacy API contract.

whole_original_hunk_reviews.decision: The modern MDC option replaces ComponentHarness with ContentContainerComponentHarness, exposing additional public loader methods. The untouched legacy option keeps its original parent and exact six methods; actual packed protocol cases reject changing that parent.
The added import records the modern public parent dependency. The owned historical option contract does not acquire that dependency or modify an original API golden.
The modern public guard changes the option parent. This is a real public API expansion, not an inherited legacy fix; actual packed prototype and method-set checks preserve Material 16.

reviews.decision: The current21.2.14public CDK supplies the two loader methods, and current public input/native-select/datepicker label lookup accepts legacy label bindings without the initial MDC prefix. The owned input adapter preserves predicate identity/native disabled behavior. The owned legacy select retains its finite disabled-only filter and old parent; modern select label API is not copied. Upstream fixture/doc edits are source review, not execution of those suites.

whole_original_hunk_reviews.decision: The public loader interface gains indexed lookup and counting. The installed 21.2.14 CDK declares these stable methods; the packed legacy button inherits them through its existing content-container parent. No CDK interface or implementation is copied.

The new content-container method delegates indexed lookup to its root loader. Actual minimum-peer execution covers content/document separation, filtered indexing, bounds errors, query failures and fresh content state.
The new count method delegates to the root loader; the adjacent hasHarness edit corrects documentation spelling only. Actual minimum-peer counts cover filters, zero results and document siblings.

The new environment lookup checks a negative offset and an offset beyond the filtered result length before returning the indexed harness. The actual public environment executes each boundary and rejection case; this does not qualify browser stabilization.
The new count operation returns the locator result length. Actual public execution verifies filtered, empty and newly changed content; no independent CDK fork is introduced.

The table documents indexed lookup, count and hasHarness and generalizes the predicate wording. The public methods are covered by the minimum-peer protocol cases; upstream documentation is read rather than executed.
This import enables an added upstream form-field label fixture. It is not an owned legacy fixture change or evidence that this upstream suite ran.

The third fixture changes the expected harness count and adds a label filter assertion. Our actual current public range harness label/predicate cases cover legacy and modern labels; this upstream suite is not claimed executed.

The added modern form-field/date-range template supplies the label example. Consumer and owned Material-16 templates stay unchanged; the public minimum range harness is exercised with explicit legacy label records.
The new module import belongs only to that upstream fixture. Current source validation and protocol execution do not claim its Angular fixture lifecycle.

The initial private label selector requires MDC classes. Do not transplant it: untouched legacy labels use mat-form-field-label. The current minimum public successor is prefix-free and passes the actual legacy label cases.
The added label predicate is inherited from the current public range harness; existing value behavior is not replaced locally. Actual predicate acceptance and rejection run against legacy labels.

The original copied getter uses an MDC-prefixed id/for query. Its original implementation is replayed and fails the legacy label controls, while the current minimum successor passes id, for, aria-label precedence and missing-label behavior.
The public datepicker-input filter now extends the shared label filter. This remains a current peer surface; no label interface or modern form-field implementation is copied into the add-on.
The public range-input filter adds the same label contract. The peer range harness predicate is exercised on legacy label records, with the supplied legacy templates preserved.
The import changes to the public form-field control harness base. The installed minimum exports that stable base; the peer datepicker hierarchy is consumed without recreating its implementation.

The new label predicate and parent class provide the minimum-peer getter behavior. Actual datepicker-input label and predicate execution covers the supported legacy label paths without copying the initial MDC query.
The added form-field/input imports support only an upstream fixture expansion. No owned module or consumer import is changed by this source review.
The new label-filter test is reviewed as upstream intent. Independent current public datepicker-input predicate cases execute the legacy id/for label behavior; this upstream suite is not claimed run.

The old input/date-picker test fixture is wrapped with a form-field and label and imports the associated modules. It is a test-only change; original add-on templates and historical suite assertions are retained.

This new public interface adds an optional label predicate. Its minimum-peer declarations and label predicate behavior are checked; no modern form-field API mirror or new owned declaration is introduced.

The entire new base/getter is reviewed. Its initial MDC-only selector cannot satisfy legacy labels, so that code is not copied. The actual stable minimum successor uses unprefixed queries and passes both legacy and modern label records; the original MDC reversion controls fail as expected.

The new filter export belongs to the peer testing entry point. The minimum public namespace is authenticated and consumed through existing peer parents/aliases; the add-on export surface is not expanded by a copied declaration.

The current public input filter inherits the shared label criterion. The existing owned input adapter consumes its public parent/filter identity; independent legacy label predicates run on the actual packed adapter.

This replaces a length assertion with the new public loader count method while preserving the expected count. The actual minimum method is exercised independently; original upstream tests are not reported as executed.
The value assertion remains and a label filter case is added. Actual packed input predicate acceptance and wrong-label rejection cover the legacy label path.
The added explicit label is an upstream fixture-only change. The untouched legacy label structure supplies our independent expectations; no consumer or owned HTML change is made.

The public input changes parent to the new shared base. The packed legacy input retains the exact current public input parent; independent current minimum declarations and prototype identity are checked.

The new label predicate is exercised through the actual packed legacy input/current parent. Legacy id/for labels and accessibility precedence work with the current successor; no MDC-only getter is copied.
Only the native-select filter gains the shared label criterion; the native-option filter still uses BaseHarnessFilters. The legacy native-select export remains the genuine current peer identity.
The new label-filter test states upstream intent. The independent current native-select alias executes label predicate acceptance and rejection with legacy label records.
The explicit label is confined to an upstream test fixture. Existing legacy component structure/styles and consumer templates stay unchanged.
The import changes to the shared public control harness base. Its current minimum export is authenticated; no private or compatibility-only symbol is used.
The native-select parent now supplies label behavior. The add-on keeps its peer alias identity and inherits the current prefix-free successor.
The added static predicate calls getLabel. Actual public native-select predicates run against legacy id/for labels, including wrong-label rejection.
This adds a modern select label filter. Do not adopt it: the owned legacy select intentionally retains its historical disabled-only filter and no getLabel contract.
The new modern-select label test is outside the finite owned legacy testing API. The packed legacy filter/no-getLabel assertions demonstrate the exclusion; this upstream test is not reported run.
The extra modern form-field label is an upstream fixture change and is not copied to the owned legacy select or any consumer HTML.

The modern select changes core testing imports and its form-field base. The owned legacy select remains independently owned with its existing option harnesses and historical parent; no modern import/parent migration is copied.
The modern select preserves disabled filtering and adds label filtering. The owned legacy filter remains disabled-only, as verified against actual packed source and public API behavior.

reviews.decision: The four-file change adds modern buttonType/getType API. The packed owned legacy harness preserves raised/flat/stroked variants, its finite historical filter interface and native text predicate. Adding a new modern button API is outside this finite legacy contract.

whole_original_hunk_reviews.decision: The modern API adds buttonType and ButtonType; the finite owned legacy filter remains text/variant/disabled. No candidate expectation or original golden is rewritten.
The modern getType getter is new API. The owned legacy harness keeps its historical getVariant and no getType promise.
The new ButtonType union belongs to modern button API and is not added to the legacy interface.
The new buttonType filter is outside the historical filter surface; actual packed interface checks retain the finite three original filters.
The expected count increases for one new modern submit-button fixture, not an owned behavior fix.
The enabled count changes for that added fixture; no historical expected count is adjusted.
The new submit-button filter/getType assertion exercises new modern API. The owned packed harness explicitly lacks this method/filter.
The expected variant list gains the newly added basic button; the owned raised/flat/stroked variants remain their historical meanings.
The appearance list adds the new modern text appearance; no modern appearance model is copied to the legacy harness.
The submit-button template fixture is upstream-only. No owned or consumer HTML change is required.
The import adds the modern ButtonType declaration; the legacy harness imports no such type.
The buttonType predicate is new modern functionality and is not copied into the legacy with() method.
The full getter maps the type attribute to a finite union or null. It adds a new method rather than repairing an original legacy promise, so it is excluded.

reviews.decision: The five-file change adds iconName and a MatIconHarness dependency to modern buttons. The owned historical filter has no iconName promise or icon-harness import. Its text/variant predicates and inherited content-container behavior remain separate. No new icon predicate or Bazel dependency is copied.

whole_original_hunk_reviews.decision: The new iconName filter is absent from the original owned contract; the historical API golden is preserved.
The MatIconHarness target is needed only by the new modern iconName predicate. The owned button has no corresponding icon/testing edge.
The added string/RegExp iconName criterion is excluded from the finite legacy filter interface.
The new named-icon search tests modern content querying. The actual packed legacy harness retains its text/variant predicates without adding this API.
The new MatIconHarness dependency is not copied into the owned harness. The owned legacy testing surface and its existing selectors remain unchanged.
The new hasHarness iconName predicate is excluded, while unrelated public content-container methods remain their genuine existing peer implementation.

reviews.decision: The five-file change adds modern no-data row/cell harness classes and getNoDataRow with an MDC row selector. The packed legacy table retains its finite row/cell harnesses and ordered cell-text behavior. This testing-API decision makes no change to the legacy no-data component or its markup.

whole_original_hunk_reviews.decision: The two no-data harness classes are new modern testing API, outside the finite owned row/cell surface.
The getNoDataRow method is new API; the legacy table does not promise it. The owned legacy testing surface and its existing selectors remain unchanged.
The entire MatNoDataCellHarness class is new modern API. Existing owned legacy cell selectors, text behavior and predicates remain unchanged.
The new no-data cell import belongs only to the new modern row harness. The owned legacy testing surface and its existing selectors remain unchanged.
The new row uses an MDC row selector and a new cell harness. Neither class is copied or adapted; the existing legacy no-data component itself is unaffected.
The signal import supports a new modern testing fixture, not a production table change.
The new empty-data row lookup asserts newly added modern harness APIs; independent packed legacy row/cell behavior is covered without this API expansion.
The template switches to a signal call and adds a no-data row fixture. Neither the owned template nor its historical expected output is modified.
The data-source initializer is wrapped in a signal for that fixture; no owned data-source implementation changes.
The new row-harness import is outside the finite legacy table harness dependency graph.
The locatorForOptional getNoDataRow method adds modern API. Actual packed legacy row/cell order is checked and the new method/classes are absent.

reviews.decision: This one-file follow-up changes the newly added modern iconName predicate from hasHarness to locatorForOptional. The owned legacy button implements neither that filter nor that query path; its separately qualified content-container methods are inherited from public CDK.

whole_original_hunk_reviews.decision: The iconName predicate changes from hasHarness to locatorForOptional and a null check. Since the owned legacy button implements neither iconName nor MatIconHarness querying, this follow-up has no applicable owned behavior.

reviews.decision: The one-file research-head decorator replacement requires Service, which is absent from the21.xframework public namespace. The actual21.2.14public FakeMatIconRegistry injects and keeps its font-alias behavior using the installed framework. The owned production source graph has no icon/testing delegation to port; no younger peer or Service shim is introduced.

whole_original_hunk_reviews.decision: The import replaces Injectable with the newer Service API. Service is absent from the advertised 21.x framework namespace; no younger peer or shim is introduced.

The decorator changes to Service({autoProvided:false}). The existing public 21.2.14 FakeMatIconRegistry constructs through the actual public Injector and preserves its fake font behavior; the owned production graph has no icon/testing delegation to port.
